headline: Rand past R17/$ after October CPI of 5.2%; September retail sales growth slows to 2.4%
summary: The rand weakened 0.8% to R17.07 per dollar at 12:00 SAST on Wednesday, after Stats SA reported October inflation of 5.2% (September 4.5%) and core inflation of 4.2% (September 4.0%) (Bloomberg via BusinessTech, 18 Nov 2026); Stats SA also reported September retail sales up 2.4% year on year, slower than August's 3.2% (EWN, 18 Nov 2026). In the US, Nvidia shares rose 4.1% to $161.90 in after-hours trade on Tuesday after its results beat estimates, following a 1.0% fall in the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, 17 Nov 2026). Gold slipped below $3,800 an ounce after Federal Reserve officials argued for further rate hikes, which Bloomberg named as the main pressure on the rand; the SARB announces its decision on Thursday with the repo rate at 7.25%.

items.title: Nvidia quarterly revenue $115.8bn, ahead of the $108.7bn consensus; guides to $130bn
items.summary: Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8bn for the quarter to October, up 20% from $96.2bn in the previous quarter and about 103% from $57.0bn a year earlier. That is about 6.5% above the average analyst estimate of $108.7bn. For the fourth quarter, which includes an extra week, the company expects revenue of $130.0bn plus or minus 3% and gross margins of 71%-72%, and assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China.
items.source: NVIDIA Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR), filed 17 Nov 2026, read by LRC Research 18 Nov 2026 06:47 SAST; consensus from LRC Earnings Calendar (market data feed, 42 estimates), 17 Nov 2026

items.title: October CPI 5.2% year on year, up from 4.5%; core inflation 4.2%
items.summary: Stats SA's consumer price index rose 5.2% year on year in October against 4.5% in September, and 0.7% on the month. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, rose to 4.2% from 4.0%, below the roughly 4.5% Nedbank had expected before the release. The headline figure matched the median of 15 economists in a Bloomberg survey and the 5.2% Reuters poll.
items.source: Stats SA October 2026 CPI via Bloomberg (BusinessTech), 18 Nov 2026; InstaForex, 18 Nov 2026 10:00 SAST; Nedbank via CNBC Africa (Reuters), 18 Nov 2026

items.title: September retail sales up 2.4% year on year, slower than August's 3.2%
items.summary: Stats SA said retail trade sales grew 2.4% year on year in September 2026, down from 3.2% in August, and fell 0.3% on the month (seasonally adjusted), the second monthly decline in a row. General dealers were the biggest contributor to annual growth; hardware, paint and glass retailers fell 1.5% year on year. Slower spending growth sits alongside higher inflation ahead of Thursday's SARB decision.
items.source: Stats SA September 2026 retail trade sales via EWN (Anelitha Fandese), 18 Nov 2026 12:08 SAST

items.title: SARB decides on Thursday; markets expect no change
items.summary: The SARB announces its decision on Thursday 19 November with the repo rate at 7.25% after September's 25bp hike. Most economists expect the rate to be left unchanged (Bloomberg; Reuters). The benchmark 2035 government bond yield was 8.625% early on Wednesday.
items.source: Reuters via CNBC Africa, 18 Nov 2026 08:53 GMT; LRC Macro Desk (SARB), 17 Nov 2026

items.title: Rand weakens 0.8% to R17.07/$, past the R17 mark
items.summary: The rand traded at R17.07 per dollar at 12:00 SAST on Wednesday, 0.8% weaker on the day and the second-worst performer among currencies Bloomberg tracks. It was at R16.98 at 07:05 SAST and R16.76 at Friday's close. Bloomberg linked the move mainly to gold falling below $3,800 an ounce after Federal Reserve officials argued for more rate hikes; TP ICAP's Devon Pearman said inflation running above some expectations 'may partially' explain it. On Tuesday TreasuryONE's Wichard Cilliers called R17 the rand's weakest level since April.
items.source: Bloomberg via BusinessTech, 18 Nov 2026 (12:00 SAST level); Reuters via CNBC Africa, 17-18 Nov 2026; LRC Market Dashboard (Yahoo Finance ZAR=X), Friday close 13 Nov 2026

items.title: Nvidia results above estimates; shares +4.1% after hours; our rating unchanged
items.summary: Nvidia closed Tuesday at $155.46 (-0.4%) and traded at $161.90 (+4.1%) after hours following results that beat estimates. AMD and Broadcom rose more than 1% after hours. Morningstar's Brian Colello described the quarter as 'business as usual' with an encouraging forecast. Nvidia is on the LRC Investment watchlist (grade A); the scanner rating is not changed by this note.
items.source: Yahoo Finance (Ines Ferré), 17 Nov 2026 14:25 PST; Nvidia quote at 19:44 EST, 17 Nov 2026; LRC Watchlist, 14 Nov 2026
